# Benchmarks and evaluation resources
[Overview](../README.md) · [Evaluation guide](evaluation-guide.md)
These are benchmark papers, not a count of independently inspected dataset releases. A code link does not certify completeness or reproduce a score. Memory recall and sustained improvement measure different outcomes.
| Work | What it tests | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [The Right Fact, the Wrong Decision: SciValidityBench for Scientific Agent Memory](papers.md#scivaliditybench) | Evaluates 64 task specifications across five validity modules, six domains, and four model families, with counterfactual, repair, and serialization controls. | Histories and clinical scenarios are synthetic, and compilation rules are supplied. Effects vary by reader and module; richer state sometimes hurts. Curator interpretation: this evaluates state use, not autonomous discovery of validity rules or continual learning in deployed scientists. |
| [PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents](papers.md#past-bench) | Tests personal-agent frameworks across memory, procedural reuse, information gathering, and update, with diagnostic interventions in Hermes+. | The controlled families and model-dependent gains test prerequisites for recursive improvement, not an open-ended recursive process. Task scores and intended mechanism evidence are separate outcomes. |
| [GDPevo: Evaluating Agent Self-Evolution on Real Business Tasks](papers.md#gdpevo) | Compares agent/model combinations and supervision types on generated enterprise workflow tasks and analyzes rule transfer. | Construction calibrates task groups partly for an expected improvement range, which can favor detectable learning gains. These are generated business scenarios, not a live enterprise deployment study. |
| [AgentStream: How Well Do Self-Evolving LLM Agents Perform Under Streaming Tasks?](papers.md#agentstream) | Crosses five methods with three model backbones and six benchmarks; method benefits vary with the model and stream composition. | The paper limits model-strength conclusions to its framework and selected benchmarks. Streaming performance is not proof of indefinite retention or deployment reliability. |
| [LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues](papers.md#longmemeval-v2) | Compares retrieval and coding-agent evidence gathering on questions derived from specialized environments, including accuracy and latency tradeoffs. | This is a context-gathering and question-answering benchmark. Better answers do not alone demonstrate successful live task execution or sustained autonomous skill acquisition; the paper is marked work in progress. |
| [SkillFlow:Benchmarking Lifelong Skill Discovery and Evolution for Autonomous Agents](papers.md#skillflow) | Measures task success, skill discovery, revision, and reuse across a structured set of task families, with benefits differing substantially across models. | Skill invocation is not evidence of useful learning: the paper reports high use with small gains or regression. Family-specific evaluation does not establish broad transfer. |
| [Building Self-Evolving Agents via Experience-Driven Lifelong Learning: A Framework and Benchmark](papers.md#ell-stulife) | The inspected preprint v6 resets agent context between tasks; retained information must be explicitly stored and retrieved through environmental tools such as calendars and drafts. The later published abstract additionally describes context-engineering comparisons, whose full protocol was not reviewed here. | The selected full-text review concerns the preprint v6 baseline in a designed simulation, not a trained lifelong learner’s learning curve. The renamed Findings of EMNLP 2026 version has verified publication metadata; its full experimental revision was not inspected. |
| [LifelongAgentBench: Evaluating LLM Agents as Lifelong Learners](papers.md#lifelongagentbench) | Tests experience reuse and a group self-consistency mechanism; ordinary replay is limited by irrelevant context and context length. | Performance on these task sequences should be separated from general lifelong learning. The abstract does not establish a complete audit of forgetting or long-term deployment. |
| [LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory](papers.md#longmemeval) | Evaluates memory designs and downstream question answering over controlled histories with scalable length. | Recall and evidence use are components of learning agents, not direct proof of procedural improvement. History version, reader, retrieval budget, and grader must be matched for comparisons. |
| [Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents](papers.md#locomo) | Compares memory approaches on the LoCoMo conversational benchmark. | Recall from generated and edited conversations differs from learning a reusable procedure or improving an agent. Dataset statistics differ between paper and project versions; pin the artifact before comparing scores. |
